headline: 6.3m AT 97.2 g/t GOLD — OceanaGold Studies 50% Waihi Plant Expansion After Wharekirauponga's Best Holes Yet
snippet: OceanaGold (TSX/ASX: OGC) reported 16 new drill holes at Wharekirauponga in New Zealand's Waihi District, with the best interval grading 6.3 metres at 97.2 g/t gold — among the highest grades drilled at the deposit to date. The company is now evaluating a 50% increase in Waihi processing capacity from 800,000 to 1.2 million tonnes per year to allow the Martha underground mine and Wharekirauponga to operate concurrently, with an updated technical report due in January 2027.

headline: 0.90m AT 1,469 g/t SILVER — Minaurum Step-Outs Hit Four Separate Veins in Phase II 50,000m Alamos Campaign
snippet: Minaurum Silver (TSXV: MGG) released step-out drilling results from its ongoing Phase II 50,000-metre resource expansion program at the Alamos Silver Project in Sonora, Mexico, hitting high grades across four separate vein zones: 0.90m at 1,469 g/t AgEq (including 0.50m at 2,425 g/t AgEq) at San Jose, 0.50m at 1,559 g/t AgEq at Quintera, and 3.40m at 397 g/t AgEq at Europa Sur. The Quintera and Travesia veins will enter the next resource update, while early Promontorio Sur step-outs point to an additional resource growth corridor 200 metres south of a known fault.

headline: VIKING MINES JUMPS 25% ON LINKA TUNGSTEN — 18m AT 0.42% WO3 Below Historic Nevada Mine; US-Backed Critical Mineral Play
snippet: Viking Mines (ASX: VKA) surged 25% after confirming thick tungsten mineralisation above and below the historic Linka Mine workings at its Linka project in Nevada, with the best new intervals grading 18m at 0.42% WO3 from 62m and 13m at 0.46% WO3 from 70m in its maiden RC drill program. The results come as US government backing for domestic tungsten supply accelerates due to ongoing Chinese export restrictions on the critical mineral, with seven additional holes still pending assay for mid-October results.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD HITS 7.88 g/t OVER 12.70m — Gold Rock Grows to 15 Structures; Visible Gold Found 3km Away at New Mud Lake North
snippet: Dryden Gold (TSX-V: DRY) released assay results including 12.70m at 7.88 g/t gold (including 1.90m at 46.05 g/t) between the Jubilee and Pearl high-grade zones at Gold Rock, confirming continuity across 350 metres of strike and expanding the project to 15 gold-bearing structures and 10 high-grade zones. In a separate announcement, the company also reported visible gold in its first drill holes at Mud Lake North — a new target located approximately 3 kilometres north of Gold Rock — opening a new discovery front on the property.

headline: ESCONDIDA CONTRACT EXPIRES SEPT 30 — Supervisors Union Urges No Vote; Legal Strike Could Hit World's Largest Copper Mine by Mid-October
snippet: The Sindicato N°2 supervisors and staff union at BHP's Escondida mine in Chile — representing approximately 1,020 members — unanimously rejected BHP's latest collective contract offer and is urging members to vote against it in the formal ballot scheduled September 28–30. The existing contract expires September 30; if members vote to strike, a mandatory five-day government mediation follows before a legal strike can begin, putting a potential work stoppage at the mine responsible for roughly 5% of global copper supply as early as mid-October.

headline: GREENLAND MINES DOUBLES RARE EARTH FOOTPRINT — 192 km² to 454 km² at Sarfartoq; Stock +206% on Expansion Application
snippet: Greenland Mines (NASDAQ: GRML) filed an application to the Government of Greenland for a new 262 km² exploration licence immediately east of its existing Sarfartoq Nd-Pr rare earths deposit, which would more than double the company's land position from approximately 192 km² to 454 km² across the known carbonatite district. The expansion follows the recent US-Denmark-Greenland Security Agreement and is designed to secure district-scale control around the ST1 deposit, which carries a $2.05 billion high-case NPV; shares surged 206% on the announcement.

headline: 578 g/t SILVER EQUIVALENT IN PERU — Titiminas Hits Mineralised Rock in All 12 New Holes Across Madre Sierra Vein Systems
snippet: Titiminas Silver (TSXV: TITI) reported results from 12 additional packsack drill holes at its Madre Sierra and Madre Sierra Norte projects in Peru, with every hole intersecting mineralised structures across multiple veins. Top results include 1.00m true width at 479 g/t AgEq (201.2 g/t Ag, 1.70 g/t Au, 2.36% Cu) and 0.65m at 578 g/t AgEq (107.8 g/t Ag, 5.32 g/t Au, 12.56% Zn), with the programme simultaneously expanding silver mineralisation at both the Madre Sierra Norte and Madre Sierra zones.

headline: GOLD MINERS' MOMENT — Record Cash Flows, Low Valuations Set Stage for Re-Rating as $4,300/oz Gold Holds
snippet: With gold sustaining above $4,300 per ounce despite a three-session pullback from record highs, analysts are highlighting a structural case that gold mining equities remain undervalued relative to the commodity price. Mine supply has been essentially flat since 2018 while cash margins and free cash flow have reached record levels; the combination of strong operational fundamentals and compressed multiples is drawing renewed investor focus to both producing miners and quality development projects.

headline: THE HIKE IS PRICED IN — Silver Positioning at Lows While Sixth Consecutive Annual Deficit Deepens to 46.3M oz
snippet: GoldSilver.com's September outlook argues that silver has fully absorbed the Federal Reserve's rate-hike messaging — having fallen nearly 50% from January's record high — while the structural supply deficit for 2026 (the sixth consecutive annual shortfall, forecast at 46.3 million ounces) continues to widen. The analysis identifies a positioning gap between historically low speculative net longs and record-high industrial demand from solar, EV and AI hardware sectors, a setup historically associated with sharp reversals when rate sentiment shifts.

headline: US BACKS NIGERIA'S MINERALS — Framework Deal Covers Exploration, Processing and Critical Mineral Infrastructure in West Africa
snippet: Nigeria and the United States signed a framework agreement aimed at deepening US investment in Nigeria's mining sector, covering geological data, exploration licensing, mineral development and processing, critical infrastructure, and technical capacity building. The deal is part of Washington's broader push to develop non-Chinese mineral supply chains, with Nigeria holding significant underdeveloped deposits of lithium, niobium, gold and iron ore, and with a specific focus on attracting private US capital into exploration.
